newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul to issue futures trading licences in Nov.
newsitem.headline: Seoul to issue futures trading licences in Nov.

text.p: South Korea will begin issuing licences for futures brokers in November, the Ministry of Finance and Economy said in a statement on Tuesday.
The licence will allow holders to enter the futures brokerage business both overseas and domestically, when a local futures exchange is set up. The exchange is expected to open in 1998.
The existing 10 local commodity futures brokerages, which currently are limited to overseas commodity trading, will automatically be licensed if they meet capital requirements.
The statement said applicant firms must be capitalised at over 10 billion won.
Shareholders of the futures brokerages will be limited to banks, merchant banks, securities houses, leasing and insurance companies, the ministry said.
Banks, securities houses, merchant banks and leasing firms must have more than 100 billion won in capital, while insurance companies must be capitalised at over one trillion won.
Local financial institutions unable to meet the capital requiremnts will be allowed to invest as part of a consortium.
Each of South Korea's large conglomerates will be allowed to have only one futures licence.
Foreigners will not be allowed to apply for the licence until the local futures exchange is set up.
"At the moment, we don't even have a futures exchange, so we don't think that foreigners will be interested in a licence," a finance ministry official said.
Shareholders holding stakes of over 25 percent will be required to maintain their position for three years after obtainingthe licence.
